A university registrar's office maintains data about the following entities: (a) courses, with attributes including number, title, credits, syllabus, and prerequisites; (b) course offerings, to model year, semester, section number, timings, and classroom; (c) students, with attributes student-id, name, and program; (d) instructors, with attributes identification number, name, department, qualifications and title. Further, the enrolment of students in courses and grades awarded to students in each course they are enrolled in must be appropriately modelled. Each student has exactly one instructor as a proctor. A proctor is a professor/instructor who proctors zero or more students. One or more courses are offered by an instructor, and one or more students register for a course offered by an instructor. A course can have zero or more prerequisites. The qualifications of an instructor can be many. One of the instructors is a HOD for a department. Also, the syllabus for each course is designed by one or more faculty members who are instructors. Construct an E-R diagram for the registrar's office as per the specifications. Document all other assumptions that you make about the mapping constraints (cardinality ratios).

Examine the two situations listed below, which were seen in two distinct organizations: a) A global retail company intends to introduce a feature-rich online shopping platform. Consumers will use a mobile or web interface to peruse merchandise. The system uses a number of business rules when customers place orders, including figuring out shipping costs, comparing inventory across several warehouses, applying offers, and finally storing the transaction information in a central database. Additionally, the business wishes to make sure that changes to business logic, such as discount policies, may be implemented without immediately impacting the database structure or user experience. b) A small educational university uses a lightweight software application for managing its library operations. This software is installed on each librarian's desktop, and it allows them to search for books, issue and return books, and manage student records. It does not require frequent updates, and all operations are performed within the same installed application that connects to a database maintained within the campus premises. Based on the above situations, identify which architecture is more appropriate for the situation a) and situation b). Also, justify your selection by explaining how the components interact in each situation with neat diagram and why the chosen architecture is suitable.

ABC university is developing a centralized Research Management System (RMS) to oversee all research activities. The system must store detailed information about Faculty, Research Students, Research Projects, Department and Funding Agencies. Each faculty member has unique Employee_ID, name, designation, DOB, Age, department and their contact details like email and contact number along with the location of their cabin, recorded as a combination of building name and room number. Each faculty has their own research expertise domain and relevant Research paper publication count. A faculty can undertake one or many projects and one or more Research students for the project work. Each project is identified with a unique project identifier and a project title. A project can be implemented by team members consisting of faculty and research students. Every project must be completed within stipulated time duration. RMS must maintain database of both completed and ongoing projects. Every project is sponsored by either Government or Private funding agencies. Each funding agency has an official registration number or license number assigned by the government or regulating body, name, email_id. The system also records the agency's geographical scope which specifies whether it is national level or international agency, and its organizational nature which denotes government body or managed privately. The faculty and research students involving in a project are affiliated to a specific department. Every department is given a unique identifier, name, location and contact_number(s) in the RMS. The interdisciplinary projects involve faculty and students from multiple departments. Every research student has Research_Student_ID, name, Affiliated department. Design an ER diagram for the above scenario using all appropriate types of attributes for strong/ weak entity, relationships, keys, participation existence and cardinalities which would accurately captures the system's requirements.

Design an Enhanced Entity-Relationship (EER) diagram for the following university academic management system. Your diagram should clearly specify entities, attributes (including keys), relationships, participation constraints, cardinalities, and any specialization or aggregation used. State any assumptions you make. The university manages its academic programs, courses, faculty, students, and course offerings. • The university is organized into several Faculties (e.g., Engineering, Science, Arts). Each faculty has a FacultyID, name, and dean. • Each faculty is divided into multiple Schools (e.g., School of Computer Science, School of Physics). Each school has a SchoolID, name, and head. • Each School offers several Programs (e.g., B.Tech CSE, M.Sc Physics). Each program has a ProgramID, name, duration, and degree type. • Each Program consists of multiple Courses. Each course has a CourseID, title, credits, and semester offered. • Lecturers teach courses. Each lecturer has a LecturerID, name, email, and specialization. A lecturer can teach multiple courses, and a course can be taught by multiple lecturers (possibly in different semesters). • Students enroll in one program but can register for multiple courses each semester. Each student has a StudentID, name, email, year of study, and program enrolled. • For each Course Offering (a course taught in a specific semester), record the CourseID, Semester, Year, LecturerID(s), and number of students enrolled. • Students receive grades for each course offering. Grades are recorded as A/B/C/D/F. • Some courses are electives and can be chosen by students from any program, while others are core and mandatory for specific programs. • There are specializations for students: Undergraduate and Postgraduate. Postgraduate students may have a thesis title and a supervisor (who is a lecturer). • The university tracks prerequisite relationships between courses (e.g., Course A is a prerequisite for Course B). (10 marks)
